title: DisCoMBO: Steering Expert-in-the-Loop Black-Box Optimization via Distributional Conformance
claim: A generative surrogate's conformance-based uncertainty matches kernel-based uncertainty and can judge whether external knowledge fits the model's evidence.
layout: 2 panels side by side; 1D regression plot left, 2D contour with priors right
description: Two panels. Panel (a) is a 1D line plot of objective or prediction against x. A black ground-truth curve f(x) passes through five black observation dots. A gray Gaussian-process mean with a gray uncertainty band and a crimson probabilistic-circuit mean with a pink uncertainty band both pass through the dots. Both bands pinch at the observations and widen between and beyond them. A legend sits underneath. Panel (b) is a 2D contour map over x1 and x2 with light gray contour lines, two lavender blobs marking good regions, and scattered dark observed points. Horizontal dashed bands mark expert priors. The upper pink band has a crimson density curve and a red X, meaning a misleading prior. The lower gray band has a black density curve and a green check, meaning a beneficial prior. The eye goes first to the colored curves in (a), then to the check and X marks in (b).
caption: DisCo provides uncertainty estimates for PC-based SMBO and allows for accurate conformance assessment of external knowledge – both with linear inference time. (a) Given a learned PC from observations, DisCo ( ) provides uncertainty estimates with linear inference cost based on how well a given point x conforms with the distribution represented by the PC, resulting in uncertainty quantification akin to Gaussian Processes (GPs; ). (b) DisCo can assess whether externally provided knowledge conforms to the PC’s expectation for improving upon y∗, serving as a scale-independent basis for acceptance or rejection of given knowledge.
abstract: Sequential Model-Based Optimization (SMBO) traditionally relies on Bayesian or ensembling surrogates for uncertainty quantification. While historically treated as fully data-driven, SMBO increasingly integrates external domain expertise to accelerate discovery. To overcome the opaque guidance and diminished integration fidelity of standard acquisition re-weighting, Probabilistic Circuits (PCs) have emerged as a generative surrogate alternative, enabling direct knowledge injection via conditional sampling. However, these generative routines lack the formal exploration-exploitation semantics required for rigorous optimization. We introduce the Distributional Conformance Score (DisCo), a novel metric that unifies the flexibility and efficiency of PCs with a formal uncertainty framework. DisCo provides a bounded, $[0, 1]$-normalized measure of model "surprise" that (1) recovers properties comparable to kernel-based uncertainty known from, e.g., Gaussian Processes, while maintaining linear-time inference, and (2) enables accurate assessment of conformance of external knowledge w.r.t. model evidence. We then present DisCoMBO, a framework leveraging these properties for robust, knowledge-aware optimization. We prove that DisCoMBO is a zero-regret algorithm and demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse benchmarks from AutoML, material optimization, and wind park optimization.
